title: Advanced pancreatic cancer: metformin did not improve survival

Q01.answer: Test adding metformin to gemcitabine and erlotinib. Prespecified six-month overall survival. Clinical survival benefit in advanced pancreatic cancer. Mechanistic hypotheses are secondary.

Q02.answer: Adults with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Four Dutch centers; approximately 73% metastatic; diabetes allowed. 121 randomized: 60 metformin and 61 placebo; diabetes in six and eight respectively. Not a prevention study.

Q03.answer: Oral metformin tablets. 500 mg twice daily in week one, then 1000 mg twice daily until progression or intolerance. Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days plus erlotinib 100 mg daily. Median follow-up 28.1 months. Not representative of every current pancreatic regimen.

Q04.answer: Matched placebo with identical cancer treatment. Central TENALEA allocation, stratified by hospital, diabetes and stage. Computer-generated blocks of six; block size concealed. Patients, physicians and study personnel masked. Concurrent randomized phase II comparison. Good allocation safeguards support the null comparison.

Q05.answer: Primary six-month overall survival; PFS, response and metabolic analyses secondary. Survival follow-up and RECIST response; CTCAE toxicity. Primary six months. Clinical endpoints; insulin and drug concentrations exploratory. Design sought a very large six-month survival change from 50% to 75%. Power does not establish a small-effect equivalence margin.

Q06.answer: Six-month survival 56.7% metformin versus 63.9% placebo. 60 versus 61 randomized; 52 versus 54 deaths over follow-up. Median survival 6.8 versus 7.6 months; HR 1.056, 95% CI .72–1.55. Six-month difference −7.2 percentage points, calculated from rounded estimates. Six-month P=.41; overall HR P=.78; PFS HR 1.18, CI .77–1.82. No demonstrated survival advantage.

Q07.answer: Follow-up continued after drug discontinuation. Serial plasma analysis available in selected participants, including 29 metformin recipients. Full-dose escalation in 38/60 metformin versus 49/61 placebo; dose reductions 34 versus 17. No reported postrandomization efficacy exclusion from ITT. Randomized ITT efficacy; selected biomarker subsets. Individual patient. Drug-concentration subgroups are not randomized dose comparisons.

Q08.answer: Graded treatment-emergent adverse events. 60 metformin and 61 placebo assigned. Grade 3/4 neutropenia 15 each; diarrhea six versus three; fatigue six versus two; no hypoglycemia reported. All study drugs stopped for toxicity in 13 versus eight; one metformin-only GI withdrawal and four metformin/erlotinib GI withdrawals. Median treatment 2.5 versus 4.6 months. Shorter exposure in metformin complicates direct toxicity-frequency interpretation.

Q09.answer: Small phase II trial with good masking; limited exposure and dose reductions. More performance-status-2 participants and higher CA19-9 in metformin arm; adjusted survival remained null. Separate protocol/SAP not acquired for historical endpoint comparison. Biomarker and concentration analyses exploratory and multiple. Wide HR interval permits moderate benefit or harm. One Results sentence calls placebo n=60; randomization figure and total establish 61. Preserve the discrepancy; use coherent randomized denominators.

Q10.answer: Advanced pancreatic cancer, including a small diabetic subgroup. This chemotherapy combination and conventional antidiabetic doses. Does not support a survival benefit as an add-on. Not all cancers, preventive settings or future combinations. Post hoc high-concentration survival cannot justify dose escalation.

Q11.answer: Kordes pancreatic phase II trial. Biomarker analyses are within this trial. No additional independent trial from serial drug measurements. Current guide sources only. One randomized family.

Q12.answer: Sil Kordes, Michael Pollak, Johanna Wilmink and colleagues. Academic Medical Centre and other Dutch hospitals. Academic Medical Centre and Terry Fox Foundation; stated no funder role. Commercial product supply details not confirmed in inspected text. Authors declared no competing interests. Disclosure does not substitute for design appraisal.

Q13.answer: Lancet Oncology 2015, DOI 10.1016/S1470-2045(15)00027-3. Full report acquired from author-associated institutional source. Separate protocol and appendices not recovered. NCT01210911 identified in report. No correction/retraction identified in retrieved records. November 3–4, 2026. Primary results directly inspected.

Q14.answer: Metformin as cancer treatment add-on. Contradicts expected major survival benefit. Trial data are null; mitochondrial or insulin explanations remain hypotheses. Do not imply a responsive high-dose subgroup was proven.

Q15.answer: This regimen did not improve survival. Small effects, different regimens and biologically selected groups remain separate questions. Adequately powered randomized clinical outcome trials would be needed. Not a reason to change prescribed diabetes care without clinical review.

appraisal: Blinded randomized phase II evidence shows no survival benefit and more dose modification with metformin. Exploratory exposure-response observations cannot establish that higher doses work.
